To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of the hCAR receptor in a B cell lymphoma cell line increased the efficiency of gene delivery by adenoviral vector by 5 fold and that this cell line can be used for further studies to improve the efficiency of gene therapy in B cell malignancies.

we developed a novel adenoviral receptor hCAR-EGFP hybrid, which can be used to create a model for adenova hCAR-EGF P fusion receptor in human Follicular lymphoma B-cells: a model for Adenoviral Gene Therapy for B cell Malignancies

we developed a novel fusion gene for adenoviral vector attachment to B cell malignancies and that we demonstrated that the gene therapy of B cells can be successful if the correct receptors are present on the tumor cell surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
adenoviral vectors for gene therapy of B-cell malignancies.
the development of adenovirus vectors for gene therapy of B lymphoid malignancies.
the design of adenocapsid with specific affinity to tumor cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this is the first report on adenoviral gene transfer into human B cell lymphoma cells and it demonstrates that this approach is feasible provided that correct receptors are present on the target cell surface.
adenoviral vectors can be used for gene therapy of B lymphoid malignancies, provided that the target cells are expressing appropriate receptors for adenoviral binding.
adenoviral vectors carrying a fusion gene of the EGFP and the cytoplasmatic domain of hCAR, can be used for gene therapy of B cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a novel fusion gene construct for the expression of a novel receptor for adenovirus in a B cell malignancy model and that this approach can be applied to other B cell malignancies as well.

the hCAR-EGFP receptor is a valid tool to increase the gene transfer rate of adenoviral vector to B cells and that the modified cells can be used as a model for gene therapy of B lymphoid malignancies.

adenoviruses are not suitable for gene therapy of disseminating B cell malignancies, but that the use of adenoviral gene delivery systems in combination with other viral or nonviral gene delivery systems might be a way to improve the efficacy of the gene therapy of these malignancies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to use the hCAR receptor in gene therapy of B lymphomas and other B cells derived malignancies.
adenoviral vectors can be used in gene therapy for hematologic malignancies, provided that the target cells express a high enough level of a suitable receptor.
adenoviral vectors are suitable for the development of gene therapy strategies for B cell-derived malignancies.
